authors: Kangxi Wu, Liang Pang, Huawei Shen and others
title: LLMDet: A Third Party Large Language Models Generated Text Detection Tool
note: Its reference code was run on authored controls, and its proxy calculation and classifier were ported to Go with numerical parity. The full detector was not reproduced.

authors: Yang Li, Qiang Sheng, Zhengjia Wang and others
title: Beyond the Final Actor: Modeling the Dual Roles of Creator and Editor for Fine-Grained LLM-Generated Text Detection
note: The released checkpoint was run on rewrites matched by source. It missed the rule that was set for it and was retired.

authors: Katherine Thai, Bradley Emi, Elyas Masrour and others
title: EditLens: Quantifying the Extent of AI Editing in Text
note: A pinned conversion of the authors' checkpoint was run in several screens. It did well on rewrites of general text and flagged technical documents that people wrote, so the score was not adopted.

authors: Chenjun Li, Cheng Wan, Haomiao Chen and others
title: MELD: Multi-Task Equilibrated Learning Detector for AI-Generated Text
note: A pinned checkpoint was run on technical documents. It missed the floor for text that a model polished.

authors: David Heineman, Yao Dou, Mounica Maddela and others
title: Dancing Between Success and Failure: Edit-level Simplification Evaluation using SALSA
note: Its model was run on constructed technical controls as a screen of whether an edit helps. The screen was rejected.

authors: Liyan Tang, Philippe Laban, Greg Durrett
title: MiniCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of LLMs on Grounding Documents
note: Its model was run as a screen of whether an edit keeps the meaning. It let unsafe edits through, and the screen was rejected.

authors: Seungone Kim, Juyoung Suk, Shayne Longpre and others
title: Prometheus 2: An Open Source Language Model Specialized in Evaluating Other Language Models
note: A local checkpoint was run as a judge with a rubric. The admission screen failed.

authors: Francesco Ortame, Roberto Navigli
title: Variable-size Discovery and Representation of Atomic Propositions
note: Its implementation was run to score the overlap of propositions between sentences. The screen stopped as a negative result.

authors: Dmitry Kobak, Rita González-Márquez, Emőke-Ágnes Horvát and others
title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
note: Its excess-frequency method was applied to the project's own matched documents, and its word list was read as phrase candidates. Most candidates turned out to be words of the writing task.

authors: Alex Reinhart, Ben Markey, Michael Laudenbach and others
title: Do LLMs write like humans? Variation in grammatical and rhetorical styles
note: Its comparison of corpora by grammatical and rhetorical features was the model for the first study. The two hypotheses that were frozen from it did not replicate.

authors: Swati Rallapalli, Shannon Gallagher, Ronald Yurko and others
title: Interpretable Stylistic Variation in Human and LLM Writing Across Genres, Models, and Decoding Strategies
note: Three design choices came from it: compare within a document role, treat variants of one model as one family, and hold out a family of generators.

authors: Ryuto Koike, Masahiro Kaneko, Ayana Niwa and others
title: ExaGPT: Example-Based Machine-Generated Text Detection for Human Interpretability
note: A simpler margin over nearest examples was built after it and tested. It did worse than a lexical measure and was retired; the paper's own method was not reproduced.

authors: Yassir El Attar, Esra Dönmez, Maximilian Maurer and others
title: A Systematic Analysis of Linguistic Features in AI-Generated English Text Detection Across Domains and Models
note: A small ensemble of features without a language model was built after its approach. It stayed below the floor on rewrites.

authors: Zhengyang Shan, Yukyung Lee, Sophie Hao
title: AI Writers Have a Consistent Stylometric Footprint, but AI Editors Do Not
note: The two features that it reports, lexical richness and token entropy, were tested with the project's tokenizer. Full generations moved in the paper's direction, and edits by a model did not.

authors: thinkst
title: ZipPy
note: Its compression idea was rebuilt in Go as the project's own measurement. The recorded run showed no benefit.

authors: KensioSoftware
title: Where the rules came from
note: Five of its measured sentence shapes were tried as candidate locations on labeled pages. Too many matches fell away from any marked event, and no rule followed.

authors: Ekaterina Artemova, Jason Lucas, Saranya Venkatraman and others
title: Beemo: Benchmark of Expert-edited Machine-generated Outputs
note: Its model answers edited by experts are one of the human references for `unswell trim`.

authors: Tuhin Chakrabarty, Philippe Laban, Chien-Sheng Wu
title: Can AI writing be salvaged? Mitigating Idiosyncrasies and Improving Human-AI Alignment in the Writing Process through Edits
note: Its paragraphs edited by professional writers gave the agreement between writers and the test of models as judges of writing.

authors: Masato Mita, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Masato Hagiwara and others
title: Towards Automated Document Revision: Grammatical Error Correction, Fluency Edits, and Beyond
note: Its corpus of editors' revisions was imported and checked. No model result rests on it.

authors: Gaetano Perrone, Simon Pietro Romano
title: ARB: A Matched Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark Dataset for AI-Text Detector Evaluation
note: Its rewrites matched by source were the test bed of several origin screens.

authors: Open Text Detector
title: Heterogeneous AI Spans: Human/AI Mixed Documents
note: Its documents with known replaced spans were used for a transfer screen.

authors: Nils Dycke, Marina Sakharova, Nico Daheim and others
title: 'Your AI Text is not Mine': Redefining and Evaluating AI-generated Text Detection under Realistic Assumptions
note: Its user-study documents were used to test two lexical features.

authors: Jerry999
title: AI-Writing-Effect: content-paired human / AI-rewritten conference-paper prose
note: Its paired academic paragraphs were used for origin-feature screens.

authors: TextSight
title: AI text detection: a control set that does not flatter detectors
note: Its passages were the target of a transfer of two frozen scores. Neither met both gates.

authors: Kenichiro Ando, Satoshi Sekine, Mamoru Komachi
title: WikiSQE: A Large-Scale Dataset for Sentence Quality Estimation in Wikipedia
note: A simple classifier was trained on its sentences marked as vague and tried on labeled pages. It covered too few missed events.

authors: vale-cli
title: Vale
note: Its Google and Microsoft styles were baselines in the experiment with `unswell fix`.

authors: btford
title: write-good
note: A baseline in the same experiment, and the best of the three linters there.

authors: Chantal Shaib, Tuhin Chakrabarty, Diego Garcia-Olano and others
title: Measuring AI "Slop" in Text
note: The closest study, with spans marked by professional editors. Its data was not public when the comparison with editors was made.

authors: Weixin Liang, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yining Mao and others
title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
note: The source of a limit that the project records: no language background is inferred from prose.

authors: Walter Laurito, Benjamin Davis, Peli Grietzer and others
title: AI-AI Bias: large language models favor communications generated by large language models
note: Published support for the finding that judge models prefer raw model text.

authors: Samuel Paech, Allen Roush, Judah Goldfeder and others
title: Antislop: A Comprehensive Framework for Identifying and Eliminating Repetitive Patterns in Language Models
note: The word lists of its companion project were read as candidates. They come from creative writing and did not fit documentation.

authors: Shoumik Saha, Soheil Feizi
title: Almost AI, Almost Human: The Challenge of Detecting AI-Polished Writing
note: Independent support for making no claim of origin: detectors flag lightly polished human text.

authors: WikiProject AI Cleanup
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
note: A list of constructions that editors curate. Its phrases overlap with the candidates that were tested.

authors: Liam Dugan, Alyssa Hwang, Filip Trhlík and others
title: RAID: A Shared Benchmark for Robust Evaluation of Machine-Generated Text Detectors
note: Read for its robustness dimensions, which went into the plan of partitions.

authors: Junchao Wu, Yefeng Liu, Chenyu Zhu and others
title: DetectRL-X: Towards Reliable Multilingual and Real-World LLM-Generated Text Detection
note: Read for its taxonomy of operations, which defined the operations of the controlled experiment.

authors: Guangsheng Bao, Yanbin Zhao, Zhiyang Teng and others
title: Fast-DetectGPT: Efficient Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text via Conditional Probability Curvature
note: Reviewed and not run: it needs token probabilities from a language model.

authors: Abhimanyu Hans, Avi Schwarzschild, Valeriia Cherepanova and others
title: Spotting LLMs With Binoculars: Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text
note: Reviewed and not run: it loads two large models.

authors: amperser
title: proselint
note: Listed in the audit of sources as a baseline of phrases and readability.

authors: retextjs
title: retext
note: Listed in the same audit, as a baseline of phrases and readability.

authors: textlint
title: textlint
note: Its fixer was reviewed in the audit of sources.

authors: languagetool-org
title: LanguageTool
note: Its exceptions for repetition served as controls in a pass on Unswell's own rules.

authors: Automattic
title: Harper
note: Its guards for repeated words became counterexamples in the same pass.

authors: bheijden
title: slop
note: Its audit with matched controls was read as a method reference.
